title: prefill-decode-stage-overlap-chunked-speculative-kernel-scheduler-optimizations
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end request latency and improve GPU utilization for mixed prefill+decode workloads by increasing useful overlap between prefill and decode stages while keeping KV cache correctness and predictable latency SLAs. This PR implements a set of coordinated improvements: 1) chunked prefill: split large prefill work into adaptive chunks to allow earlier decode work to start and better utilize kernel-level parallelism; 2) speculative prefill: launch speculative prefill chunks based on early token-distribution heuristics to warm KV cache and kernels ahead of confirmed tokens, with conservative fallbacks and cancelability to avoid wasted work; 3) stage overlap and scheduler changes: introduce a latency-aware kernel scheduler that prioritizes prefill chunks vs decode kernels based on per-request SLOs and estimated overlap benefit, plus continuous-batching adjustments that reduce head-of-line blocking by dynamically sizing batch windows for prefill vs decode; 4) KV cache and kernel dispatcher changes: prefetch-friendly KV cache sharding, refcount-safe speculative entries, and kernel dispatch path optimizations to batch small kernels and reduce kernel launch overhead. Implementation notes: changes are primarily in runtime scheduler and prefill manager (src/runtime/scheduler.cpp, src/runtime/prefill_manager.cpp), GPU kernel dispatcher (src/runtime/kernel_dispatcher.cu), KV cache layer (src/runtime/kv_cache.h, src/runtime/kv_cache.cpp), continuous batching module (src/runtime/batching_manager.cpp), and supporting tests and perf harness updates. The description below contains the end-to-end rationale, benchmark summary, compatibility and rollout plan, and operational controls. Benchmarks: internal perf lab canary across representative chat and instruction workloads shows median latency (p50) improvement of ~18% for mixed prefill+decode requests, p95 down ~12%, throughput up ~10-15% depending on sequence length distribution, and estimated token-cost reduction of ~6% owing to better kernel packing and reduced idle GPU cycles. Speculative prefill hit-rate is workload-dependent; with default heuristics we see ~68% useful speculation on conversational workloads during canary. Safety and correctness: speculative prefill is cancelable and never mutates persisted state until token confirmation; KV cache speculative entries are refcounted and rolled back on mismatch. Feature flags: runtime flags allow disabling speculative prefill, controlling chunk size policy (fixed|adaptive), and a conservative scheduler mode that prioritizes strict latency budgets over throughput. CI and stability: first CI run flagged a flaky perf integration test (tests/perf/prefill_pipeline.test) caused by an uninitialized timer in the canary harness; fixed in commit "fix: initialize prefill timer in perf harness" and subsequent CI passed. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 5% fleet -> 25% -> 100% with kill-switch and automatic fallback to legacy scheduler if p95 regression observed. Related work: builds on prior prefill/decode overlap PRs (see ENG-3214 family) and complements kernel micro-optimizations in recent dispatcher work. Backwards compatibility: no API changes; behavior controlled by runtime flags and default heuristics tuned to be conservative. Release notes: improve prefill-decode overlap through chunked and speculative prefill and latency-aware kernel scheduling; see docs/notes/prefill-decode-optimizations.md for operator guidance.

review_comments: David Kim: Can you clarify how chunk size adapts under high variability of sequence lengths? Response: chunk size uses a moving quantile estimator of inflight prefill token counts with min/max bounds; details added to comments and docs.

Priya Singh: I saw a small memory bump in canary — did you find the root cause? Response: yes, initial implementation kept speculative KV entries pinned; switched to refcounted speculative entries and added periodic GC in kv_cache.cpp which resolved the bump.

Luca Moretti: Suggest adding a conservative scheduler mode flag for latency-sensitive customers. Response: added runtime flag 'scheduler.mode=conservative' that disables speculation and favors p95 targets; described in docs.
David Kim: CI failed on perf test initially, can you add a regression test? Response: added a deterministic perf harness path and unit coverage for chunk manager to prevent regressions.
Priya Singh: Approve after addressing test flakes and adding metrics. (approved)
release_notes: Improves prefill-decode pipeline overlap with chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and latency-aware kernel scheduling; p50 latency down ~18% and p95 down ~12% in canary on mixed workloads; rollout controlled by runtime flags and canary metrics.
